newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to Jan 25.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to Jan 25.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 23.4 percent decline in its turnover during the week ending January 25 and traders blamed tight liquidity for the drop.
Total BSE turnover stood at 33.852 million dinars ($6.27 million) in 156 transactions, down on 44.211 million dinars in 170 transactions a week ago.
"Liquidity of the banking sector and the entire system is very poor. No fresh money is coming to the market. Most deals are based on revolving old borrowing," a trader told Reuters.
Despite tight liquidity, BSE performed fairly well due to rising interest for wheat contracts, BSE spokesman Milko Stimac said.

"Wheat contracts are undoubtedly a lucrative investment. Key buyers are hedgers -- flour mills. Their interest would be even greater if they had more dinars for such an investment," BSE commodities specialist Goran Altaras told Reuters.
Buying activity was gaining momentum ahead of February 3, when the two-month sale of the current tranche of wheat contracts expires, traders said.
For the week ending Jan 25, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 128 times for a volume of 16.805 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted for 14 transactions worth 1.432 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 331 and 520 percent, while maturity stretched between six and 30 days.
* There were 11 deals in wheat contracts totalling 15.295 million dinars.
* BSE reported no trade in central bank short-term bonds.
* Presenting a more detailed report of over-the-counter activity, BSE said OTC volume stood at 19.241 million dinars.
Out of 12 member brokerages, one reported a 16.14 million dinars turnover. Three more brokers accounted for the remainder. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
